labels: the macro print of the samara on the soil; keep the camera, the framing, the soil, the light and the background exactly as they are.
the film's maple seedling print (how the seedling is drawn).
prompt: Make one image: Image 1 a few days later, same camera, same framing, same soil and background, same print style. The samara has germinated where it lies: its split husk and the curled wing still rest on the soil; from the seed a pale root goes down into the soil, and a slender reddish-green stem (hypocotyl) stands straight up from it, carrying two long narrow strap-shaped seed leaves (maple cotyledons) spread open like a V, backlit gold-green against the low sun from the upper left; a tiny pair of first true leaves is just appearing between them. The seedling is in the middle of the frame and reaches about the upper third. No people, no text, no seals, no signatures.
